source.title: Feature Geometry of LoRA Adapters: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis of Representational Divergence in Fine-Tuned Language Models

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares reconstruction of LoRA-induced activation deltas by pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs and adapter-specific SAEs. This bears on whether SAE reconstruction error can shrink when the SAE is trained for the target activations, but it does not analyze the error vector's predictability or token-level behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper reports reconstruction errors for Gemma Scope and delta-specific SAEs on LoRA activation deltas, and their improvement comparison; these are recorded below for V6. Its cosine, principal-angle, CKA, feature-overlap, and delta-norm results concern adapter/base representational geometry rather than the structure of SAE reconstruction errors. No result tests linear predictability of reconstruction errors, error norms across SAE sizes, effects on model loss, or error contributions to circuits or steering.
record.test_reason: The study applies base-model Gemma Scope SAEs to LoRA activation deltas, which are differences between activations and lie outside the SAEs' training distribution. It then compares them with SAEs trained on those deltas. This measures distribution mismatch, not the dark matter of an SAE on its own training distribution. It does not examine error predictability, scaling, loss effects, or the error's role in circuits. It does not vary sparsity penalty, architecture or objective, so the V6 question (training artifact versus model structure) is not addressed. The paper does not cite the dark-matter work. Its SAE error results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right. The authors conclude that LoRA adapters occupy a feature subspace geometrically separated from base SAE features, based on cosine similarity, principal angles and CKA. They report that delta-specific SAEs achieve 46–86% lower reconstruction error than Gemma Scope on held-out deltas. They infer a monitoring gap: base-model SAEs may be blind to adapter contributions.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a pretrained base-model SAE with SAEs trained specifically on LoRA activation deltas; it does not reproduce the original dark-matter error analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction improvement varies by layer and rank; it ranges from 46.3% to 86.2%, with larger improvements in early layers. The study also reports delta SAE error increasing with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-model Gemma Scope SAEs give relative reconstruction error above 1.0 on LoRA activation deltas (1.13–2.46). SAEs trained on the deltas reach 0.34–0.65 on held-out deltas (Tables 5–7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs trained on base activations fail to reconstruct fine-tuning-induced activation deltas; delta-specific SAEs reduce but do not eliminate the error.

fits_no_version.finding: Delta-SAE held-out error plateaus after about 5–7 epochs (about 0.34 at layer 5, about 0.61 at layer 38). The authors call this possibly irreducible and resistant to sparse decomposition (Section 6.2). This is qualitative and concerns delta inputs only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual SAE error on adapter deltas persists with longer training and grows with depth.

record.problems: Single Gemma-2-9B base model, one Alpaca dataset, and one training seed. The authors say adapters were undertrained and produced outputs identical to the base model on test prompts. They report no base-base SAE similarity baseline. The tested errors are on adapter activation deltas, not a study of the error-vector properties in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for Table 7's derived percentage improvements; those values are noted alongside each paired error comparison. Other reported geometric measurements do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: All. No variation of sparsity penalty, shrinkage, dead latents, architecture or end-to-end training on the SAE's own activation distribution.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are dropped. Gemma Scope's poor fit to activation differences reflects an input distribution it was never trained on; it says nothing about whether ordinary dark matter is a training artifact. The Table 12 ablation reports reconstruction error of about 0.000022 at layer 5, rank 4, against 0.340 in Table 6, so the error metrics are inconsistent or differently defined. Other limitations: single seed and a single dataset. The adapters are undertrained, producing outputs identical to the base model on test prompts. There is no base-base SAE similarity baseline.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the SAE error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Whether per-token error norms are predictable across SAE sizes, larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, or error persists with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction errors harm model loss more than random errors of the same size.
Whether linear and nonlinear error components correspond to unlearned features and qualitatively different structure resistant to dictionary learning.
Whether omitting the error term from SAE-feature-based analyses loses model behavior.

The study compares pretrained and adapter-specific SAEs on adapter-induced deltas, but does not isolate sparsity penalty, shrinkage, dead latents, or objective effects; test alternative architectures or end-to-end training; or establish that most dark matter is a training artifact rather than structure in ordinary model activations.
